initiative.title: Plan views: 2D plan, 3D pane, and height layers
initiative.summary: How the garden is drawn and edited: watercolor 2D plan with height hints, synced 3D pane, and a layer slicer for plants under other plants.
initiative.next_action: Build the 2D renderer (scaffold, model, plants, renderer, editor, gallery).

sources.anchor: dictation on heights and layers in the 2D plan
round: 10 questions on 2D renderer and plants

claims.statement: 2D plan on the left and a 3D pane on the right, kept in sync.
The 2D plan uses artificial depth, such as shadows and shading, to hint at height; the 3D pane shows real heights and ground steps.
When plants do not overlap, a plain top view is correct even though height is not readable.
When plants sit under other plants, a layer slicer on the 2D plan shows one height band at a time.
Below the canopy, a tree shows as its trunk footprint with a shaded area, so plants under it are easy to edit.
The layer control appears only when the design has overlapping heights; flat formal designs never show it.
Editing must stay easy; never make the user look through foliage to reach plants.
Fixed layers vs free height slider is unsettled.
The ground is flat in 2D; no slope, terraces, or layers for now. Heights are only object values for shade and 3D.
First real build: 2D renderer with editing and a plant gallery, reading typed JSON property files.
Look: semi-realistic watercolor, like a hand-drawn landscape architecture plan.
Plantings are single positions, regions of one plant, or rows; the choice is per placement.
Model: lot outline, size, heading; house outline only; fences solid/semi-open/open with shade; hedges as rows; surfaces, structures, edges, garden features.

shape.appetite: One renderer, editor, and gallery; 25 plants; two property files.
shape.recommended_shape: Solid app; typed JSON property and plant files; canvas watercolor paint layer under an SVG edit layer; regions expanded to plants from spacing and seed.
success_moves: Canvas paint layer plus SVG interaction layer.
Store regions, not every plant; expand from spacing and seed.
One JSON file per plant with a validation check, so a colleague can add plants safely.
Flat ground only; heights as attributes.

first_proof.question: Does a property file render as a believable hand-drawn watercolor plan that is easy to edit across seasons and years?
first_proof.artifact: Local app showing the sample lot with a coneflower region, a redbud, and the time slider.
first_proof.decision_rule: If it looks like a hand-drawn plan and regions are easy to edit, trace Byron yard and add plants; otherwise run S5 before more editor work.

history.event: Split from the garden design app intent; heights and layers recovered from dictation.
10 questions answered; 2D renderer shape written; build starts.
